issuing_body: King, on the advice of the National Legislative Assembly
title_original: Energy Industry Act B.E. 2550 (2007)

summary_english: The framework law for the power and gas sectors. It separates policy, regulation and operation, creates the Energy Regulatory Commission (ERC) and the Power Development Fund, and sets the licence regime, with exemptions by Royal Decree (s.47). It obliges network owners to allow access under published codes (s.81), the legal basis for third-party access.
notes: Scouted from desk research (high confidence). Thai title to be added. Given 9 Dec B.E. 2550 (2007); published in the Government Gazette Vol. 124 Part 89 Kor on 10 Dec 2007; in force the next day (s.2). No enacted amendment found; amendment proposals exist. issuing_body: King (Royal Decree under s.47 of the Energy Industry Act)
title_original: Royal Decree prescribing energy industry operations exempt from licensing B.E. 2552 (2009)
title_english: Royal Decree prescribing energy industry operations exempt from licensing B.E. 2552 (2009)
summary_english: Exempts small energy operations from the ERC licence under s.47 of the Energy Industry Act. Generation under 1,000 kVA reportedly needs no licence, but the operator must still notify the ERC.
notes: Scouted from desk research (low confidence). Thai title to be added. Secondary source only (WFW guide 2018). A 2010 clarification for off-grid in-plant systems is reported. Exact title, signing date, date in force and any later amendments not confirmed; check the Royal Gazette.

title_original: Thailand Power Development Plan 2018-2037 (PDP2018)
title_english: Thailand Power Development Plan 2018-2037 (PDP2018)
summary_english: The national power development plan for 2018-2037. It planned about 56 GW of new capacity, for 77,211 MW in total by 2037. It was replaced by PDP2018 Rev.1 in 2020.
notes: Scouted from desk research (high confidence). Thai title to be added. Approved at NEPC meeting 1/2562 on 24 Jan 2019 (EPPO resolutions portal). Cabinet approval reported in May 2019 (date not confirmed); date_in_force left empty until checked.

title_original: Thailand Power Development Plan 2018-2037, Revision 1 (PDP2018 Rev.1)
title_english: Thailand Power Development Plan 2018-2037, Revision 1 (PDP2018 Rev.1)
summary_english: Revision of PDP2018, considered by the NEPC in March 2020, and still the plan in force. It plans about 20,766 MW of renewables by 2037. The draft PDP2024 was never adopted, and the draft PDP2026 (2026-2050) went to public hearing on 8 Sep 2026.
notes: Scouted from desk research (high confidence). Thai title to be added. Considered at NEPC meeting 1/2563 (150) on 19 Mar 2020; IEA says published 2020. Renewables figure from Chambers 2026. Later Cabinet step not confirmed; date_in_force left empty. Link basis not checked against the text: the report says it amends or replaces the earlier row.

title_original: Alternative Energy Development Plan 2018-2037 (AEDP2018)
title_english: Alternative Energy Development Plan 2018-2037 (AEDP2018)
summary_english: Sets the renewable energy targets that go with PDP2018 Rev.1. It was put to the NEPC on 19 Mar 2020 together with the Energy Efficiency Plan 2018 and the Gas Plan 2018.
notes: Scouted from desk research (medium confidence). Thai title to be added. Listed as a draft for consideration at NEPC 1/2563 (150) on 19 Mar 2020. The approval outcome is not confirmed; check the resolution PDF and set status to draft if it was not approved. date_in_force left empty.

title_original: NEPC resolution on guidelines for promoting rooftop solar generation
title_english: NEPC resolution on guidelines for promoting rooftop solar generation
summary_english: Sets guidelines for promoting rooftop solar, with a 90 MW residential quota to 2030. It probably raised the household buy-back rate from THB 1.68 to THB 2.20/kWh from 2021. It was amended by the NEPC's April 2026 household rooftop resolution.
notes: Scouted from desk research (low confidence). Thai title to be added. Title confirmed on the EPPO portal only. IEEFA (2026) reports the rate rise to THB 2.20/kWh in 2021; that this resolution made the change is likely but unconfirmed. The 2019 'Solar for Thai People' ERC regulation still needs a row (title not confirmed). date_in_force taken as the meeting date.

title_original: NEPC resolution on the electricity tariff structure policy of Thailand 2021-2025
title_english: NEPC resolution on the electricity tariff structure policy of Thailand 2021-2025
summary_english: Sets the tariff structure policy for 2021-2025, the framework under which the ERC sets base tariffs and the Ft adjustment. It was replaced by the 2026-2030 policy in July 2026.
notes: Scouted from desk research (medium confidence). Thai title to be added. Title confirmed on the EPPO portal. date_in_force taken as the meeting date.

title_original: NEPC resolution on feed-in tariff rates for renewable power 2022-2030
title_english: NEPC resolution on feed-in tariff rates for renewable power 2022-2030
summary_english: Sets feed-in tariff rates for 2022-2030 in THB/kWh: biogas 2.0724, ground-mounted solar 2.1679, solar with battery storage 2.8331 and wind 3.1014. Projects in the southern border provinces get THB 0.50/kWh more.
notes: Scouted from desk research (high confidence). Thai title to be added. Revised principles at NEPC 7/2565 on 7 Nov 2022 (not a separate row yet). date_in_force taken as the meeting date.

title_original: NEPC resolution postponing the retirement of Mae Moh lignite units 8-11
title_english: NEPC resolution postponing the retirement of Mae Moh lignite units 8-11
summary_english: Postpones the retirement of units 8-11 at EGAT's Mae Moh lignite plant, keeping them running to the end of 2025 because of high LNG prices. The NEPC extended units 8 and 11 further in August 2025.
notes: Scouted from desk research (medium confidence). Thai title to be added. Title confirmed on the EPPO portal; end-2025 date from The Nation. date_in_force taken as the meeting date.

title_original: ERC Regulation on procurement of renewable electricity under the FiT scheme 2022-2030 for the group without fuel costs B.E. 2565 (2022)
title_english: ERC Regulation on procurement of renewable electricity under the FiT scheme 2022-2030 for the group without fuel costs B.E. 2565 (2022)
summary_english: Sets up procurement of up to 5,203 MW of renewable power at the 2022-2030 feed-in tariff: biogas 335 MW, wind 1,500 MW, ground-mounted solar 2,368 MW and solar with storage 1,000 MW. The first round selected 175 projects of about 4,852 MW.
notes: Scouted from desk research (high confidence). Thai title to be added. 27 Sep 2022 is the Government Gazette date; signing date and date in force not confirmed. MW split per Baker McKenzie. Implements link inferred from the report (same scheme, period and rates as NEPC 3/2565); check the preamble. The 2024 ERC regulation for the 3,668.5 MW round has no row yet.

title_original: NEPC resolution on guidelines for setting the Utility Green Tariff (UGT)
title_english: NEPC resolution on guidelines for setting the Utility Green Tariff (UGT)
summary_english: Creates the Utility Green Tariff, a green electricity product sold by the utilities. It sets two products: UGT1, from pooled renewables with no specified source, and UGT2, from named plants.
notes: Scouted from desk research (high confidence). Thai title to be added. Date on both the EPPO portal and the ERC slide deck hosted by BOI (30 Jul 2024). date_in_force taken as the meeting date.

title_original: NEPC resolution on additional renewable procurement (no-fuel-cost group and industrial waste) under FiT 2022-2030
title_english: NEPC resolution on additional renewable procurement (no-fuel-cost group and industrial waste) under FiT 2022-2030
summary_english: Approves a second procurement round of 3,668.5 MW at the 2022-2030 feed-in tariff rates. The NEPC deferred the round on 25 Dec 2024, after the shortlist, and resumed it with negotiations in May 2025.
notes: Scouted from desk research (high confidence). Thai title to be added. Thai press split: about 2,632 MW solar, 1,000 MW wind, 6.5 MW biogas, 130 MW industrial waste. Shortlist 16 Dec 2024; deferral by NEPC 4/2567 (170) on 25 Dec 2024 (no row; fact-finding committee set up). The ERC regulation for this round (B.E. 2567) has no row yet: title and date not confirmed. date_in_force taken as the meeting date.

title_original: ERC approval of the Utility Green Tariff 1 (UGT1) rate
title_english: ERC approval of the Utility Green Tariff 1 (UGT1) rate
summary_english: Approves the UGT1 rate of THB 4.21/kWh, sold on one-year contracts with EGAT, MEA or PEA. The tariff launched in January 2025 with 2 billion kWh offered in the first quarter.
notes: Scouted from desk research (medium confidence). Thai title to be added. ERC deck dates UGT criteria to Jan 2024 and the UGT1 rate approval to Feb 2024; sources also give July 2024 for the approval. date_in_force is the January 2025 launch (Reccessary, 24 Jan 2025). The 2026 UGT1 premium was revised (Argus), so status may be 'amended'. No document number found.

title_original: NEPC resolution on measures allowing private parties to sign direct power purchase agreements (Direct PPA)
title_english: NEPC resolution on measures allowing private parties to sign direct power purchase agreements (Direct PPA)
summary_english: Starts a Direct PPA pilot that allows data centres to buy renewable power directly from generators over the grid through third-party access, up to 2,000 MW. The NEPC widened it to industry generally and removed the cap in July 2026.
notes: Scouted from desk research (high confidence). Thai title to be added. The ERC published a draft Direct PPA Regulation and draft TPA Code on 3 Oct 2025 (eligibility: BOI-promoted data centre with at least 50 MW IT load; new renewable plant of at least 1,000 kVA without an existing PPA); final issue not confirmed, so no row yet. date_in_force taken as the meeting date.

issuing_body: Ministry of Industry (Department of Industrial Works)
title_original: Ministerial Regulation on the designation of types, kinds and sizes of factories (No. 3) B.E. 2567 (2024)
title_english: Ministerial Regulation on the designation of types, kinds and sizes of factories (No. 3) B.E. 2567 (2024)
summary_english: Takes rooftop and building-mounted solar out of the definition of a factory at any size, so no factory licence is needed. Before, systems above 1 MW needed one. ERC licences or exemptions still apply.
notes: Scouted from desk research (medium confidence). Thai title to be added. Effective 28 Dec 2024 (Tilleke & Gibbins); signing date not confirmed (December 2024 assumed in the candidate file). The base regulation it amends not confirmed.

title_original: Cabinet resolution approving a draft Ministry of Finance ministerial regulation embedding a carbon price in excise tax on oil products
title_english: Cabinet resolution approving a draft Ministry of Finance ministerial regulation embedding a carbon price in excise tax on oil products
summary_english: Approves a carbon price of THB 200/tCO2e built into the existing excise tax on oil products, including gasoline, diesel, kerosene, jet fuel, LPG and fuel oil. Excise rates are restructured so pump prices do not change.
notes: Scouted from desk research (medium confidence). Thai title to be added. Cabinet decision confirmed. Whether the Ministry of Finance ministerial regulation was gazetted, and its effective date, are not confirmed; status set to pending until found (Excise Department, Royal Gazette). The ministerial regulation needs its own row once found.

title_english: NEPC resolution on the remaining additional renewable procurement under the 2023-2030 clean power plan
summary_english: Resumes the 3,668.5 MW additional procurement round after the December 2024 deferral. It directs the ERC, EGAT, PEA, MEA and EPPO to start negotiations with the selected applicants.
notes: Scouted from desk research (medium confidence). Thai title to be added. Follow-up resolutions on 21 Aug and 27 Oct 2025 (EPPO portal) not yet rows. Link basis not checked against the text: the report says it amends or replaces the earlier row. date_in_force taken as the meeting date.

title_english: ERC Notification (No. 2) B.E. 2568 revising the PPA timeline for the 2024 additional FiT round (no-fuel-cost group)

Likely carries out NEPC 1/2568 (TH-NEPC-2025-1-FIT-ADDITIONAL) or the round set by NEPC 2/2566, but the report does not say; add an implements link once checked.

title_english: NEPC resolution revoking the earlier resolution to split the system operator from EGAT into a separate legal entity
summary_english: Revokes the earlier NEPC decision to separate the system operator from EGAT into its own legal entity. The system operator stays inside EGAT, ring-fenced.

title_english: NEPC resolution on managing Mae Moh power plant, replacing units 8-9

title_english: NEPC resolution on the Community-based Solar Power Generation Project
summary_english: Sets up a 1,500 MW community-based solar programme. Projects of up to 10 MW per site sell to MEA or PEA as very small power producers (VSPP).
notes: Scouted from desk research (high confidence). Thai title to be added. Further NEPC/EPAC resolutions on 28 Nov 2025, 15 Jul 2026 and 3 Aug 2026 (EPPO portal) may change its terms. date_in_force taken as the meeting date.

title_english: NEPC resolution on amending the Royal Decree so that data centres can be direct customers of EGAT

title_english: Cabinet resolution approving in principle the draft Climate Change Act B.E. ...
summary_english: Cabinet approved in principle the draft Climate Change Act, a framework of 205 sections in 14 chapters. The bill provides for greenhouse gas reporting, a carbon tax, a possible emissions trading scheme and a Climate Fund. It has not been enacted.
notes: Scouted from desk research (high confidence). Thai title to be added. Status draft because the Act is not enacted; the Cabinet approval in principle has no legal force of its own. Council of State review under way in May 2026. House dissolved on 12 Dec 2025, 10 days after Cabinet approval; post-election progress not confirmed. ETS mentioned by Chambers. Re-point or add a row for the Act if it is enacted.

issuing_body: King (Royal Decree under the Revenue Code)
title_original: Royal Decree issued under the Revenue Code on tax exemption (No. 805) B.E. 2569 (2026): rooftop solar deduction
title_english: Royal Decree issued under the Revenue Code on tax exemption (No. 805) B.E. 2569 (2026): rooftop solar deduction
summary_english: Gives a personal income tax deduction of up to THB 200,000 for installing on-grid home solar of up to 10 kW. The deduction runs to 31 Dec 2028.
notes: Scouted from desk research (high confidence). Thai title to be added. Gazette publication 2 Mar 2026 (The Nation); signing date and date in force not confirmed (signing may precede March). English title is our rendering.

title_original: NEPC resolution on promoting rooftop solar for households
title_english: NEPC resolution on promoting rooftop solar for households
summary_english: Sets a new household rooftop solar net-billing scheme at THB 2.20/kWh on 10-year contracts, with a 500 MW national quota (up from 90 MW) and up to 5 kW per meter. Only households are eligible. It amends the 2020 rooftop solar guidelines.
notes: Scouted from desk research (high confidence). Thai title to be added. Needs an ERC implementing notification (IEEFA, Aug 2026: still pending); MEA/PEA installer registration ran 3 Aug-30 Sep 2026. Same meeting revised residential tariff policy. Link basis not checked against the text: the report says it amends or replaces the earlier row. date_in_force taken as the meeting date.

title_original: EPAC resolution on the Utility Green Tariff 2 (UGT2, source-specific) rate
title_english: EPAC resolution on the Utility Green Tariff 2 (UGT2, source-specific) rate
summary_english: Sets the rate for UGT2, the green tariff supplied from named renewable plants under the NEPC's 2022 guidelines. The rate itself is not yet confirmed.
notes: Scouted from desk research (medium confidence). Thai title to be added. Title confirmed on the EPPO portal. Chambers says an ERC resolution made the UGT2 tariff effective from 1 May 2026, with applications expected late 2026 and service from 2027; this conflicts with the 28 May 2026 EPAC date. 2024 drafts put the rate at about THB 4.55-4.56/kWh. Status 'in force' not confirmed. The ERC tariff decision may need its own row. date_in_force taken as the meeting date.

title_original: NEPC resolution on criteria for the pilot Direct PPA for renewable power through third-party access (TPA)
title_english: NEPC resolution on criteria for the pilot Direct PPA for renewable power through third-party access (TPA)
summary_english: Opens the Direct PPA pilot beyond data centres to industry generally and removes the 2,000 MW cap. EPAC selects and supervises participants, and data centres pay security deposits for grid use.
notes: Scouted from desk research (high confidence). Thai title to be added. EPAC approved principles on 3 Aug 2026; the ERC then consulted. Final ERC Direct PPA regulation and TPA Code not confirmed as issued (one unverified post claims Gazette publication on 14 Aug 2026). Link basis not checked against the text: the report says it amends or replaces the earlier row. date_in_force taken as the meeting date.

title_original: NEPC resolution on the electricity tariff structure policy of Thailand 2026-2030
title_english: NEPC resolution on the electricity tariff structure policy of Thailand 2026-2030
summary_english: Sets the tariff structure policy for 2026-2030, replacing the 2021-2025 policy. It adds a separate cost-reflective tariff for data centres and prices the first 200 kWh for homes at THB 3. Direct PPA buyers and data centres may pay into the Power Development Fund.
notes: Scouted from desk research (high confidence). Thai title to be added. Details from JETRO; Eco-Business reports data centres expected to pay about THB 5-6/kWh. Link basis not checked against the text: the report says it amends or replaces the earlier row. date_in_force taken as the meeting date.

title_original: ERC Regulation on procurement of electricity from community-based solar power generation projects B.E. 2569 (2026)
title_english: ERC Regulation on procurement of electricity from community-based solar power generation projects B.E. 2569 (2026)
summary_english: Sets the rules for procuring up to 1,500 MW from community-based solar projects of up to 10 MW each. Projects get a 25-year non-firm PPA with MEA or PEA at THB 2.1679/kWh, and foreign shareholding is capped at 49%.
notes: Scouted from desk research (medium confidence). Thai title to be added. 22 Sep 2026 is the Gazette date (signing date not confirmed); in force 23 Sep 2026 per law-firm summaries; Mori Hamada PDF blocked (403), details from search summaries. English title is our rendering.

title_original: Electric Power Industry Reform Act of 2001
title_english: Republic Act 9136, the Electric Power Industry Reform Act of 2001 (EPIRA)
summary_english: The framework law that restructured the power sector. It unbundled the state utility NPC, created the ERC, the WESM spot market, PSALM and TransCo, and opened generation and supply to competition while transmission and distribution stay regulated franchises. Section 31 provides for retail competition and open access.
notes: Scouted from desk research (high confidence). Approval date from the Lawphil text; date in force not found. title_original is the short title; check whether the long title should be used. Statutory amendments found so far touch only the lifeline rate (RA 10150 of 2011-06-21, not a row yet; RA 11552). EPIRA amendment bills were still pending in Congress as of 2026-07.

title_original: Act Extending and Enhancing the Implementation of the Lifeline Rate, amending Section 73 of RA 9136 as amended by RA 10150
title_english: Republic Act 11552 extending the lifeline rate
summary_english: Extends and enhances the lifeline (subsidised) electricity rate for poor households. It amends Section 73 of EPIRA (RA 9136), as already amended by RA 10150 of 2011.
notes: Scouted from desk research (high confidence). title_original comes from the candidate list and may not match the official long title word for word; check against the Lawphil text. Date in force not found. Also amends RA 10150, which is not yet a row.

title_original: Renewable Energy Act of 2008
title_english: Republic Act 9513, the Renewable Energy Act of 2008
summary_english: The framework law for renewable energy. It sets up the Renewable Portfolio Standards, feed-in tariffs, the Green Energy Option (Sec. 9) and net metering (Sec. 10).
notes: Scouted from desk research (high confidence). Approval date from Lawphil; date in force not found. title_original is the short title. Its IRR is DOE DC2009-05-0008 (not a row), amended by DC2022-11-0034 and DC2025-09-0014. Not yet checked whether the Act itself has been amended by statute.

title_original: Amending Section 19 of the Rules and Regulations Implementing RA 9513 (Renewable Energy Act of 2008)
title_english: DOE Circular DC2022-11-0034 opening renewable energy projects to full foreign ownership
summary_english: Amends Section 19 of the RE Act implementing rules (DC2009-05-0008) to allow up to 100% foreign ownership of solar, wind, hydro and ocean or tidal projects, following DOJ Opinion No. 21, s. 2022. Water permits for hydro projects stay limited to entities that are 60% Filipino-owned.
notes: Scouted from desk research (medium confidence). The official title and the DOE page were not reached (old DOE site), so title_original is descriptive; the signing date comes from Baker McKenzie and news reports. Check both against the official text. Date in force not found. The amended IRR (DC2009-05-0008) is not a row. Foreign ownership rests on a DOJ opinion and this circular rather than a law. The 'framework-law' topic fits only loosely.

title_original: Adopting and Prescribing the Policy for the Competitive Selection Process in the Procurement by the Distribution Utilities of Power Supply Agreement for the Captive Market
title_english: DOE Circular DC2018-02-0003 on competitive selection of distribution utilities' power supply agreements
summary_english: Set the policy for distribution utilities to procure power supply agreements for their captive market through a competitive selection process (CSP). DC2023-06-0021 repeals it once the ERC's companion guidelines take effect.
notes: Scouted from desk research (medium confidence). Title as given on the old DOE page and in DC2021-09-0030; the document was not fetched (legacy.doe.gov.ph unreachable). Day of signing and date in force not confirmed. The repeal by DC2023-06-0021 applies 'upon the effectivity of the ERC guidelines' (ERC Res. 16 s.2023, date not found), so check whether and when the repeal took effect.

title_original: Prescribing the Policy for the Mandatory Conduct of the Competitive Selection Process by the Distribution Utilities for the Procurement of Power Supply for Their Captive Market
title_english: DOE Circular DC2023-06-0021 on mandatory competitive selection by distribution utilities
summary_english: Makes it mandatory for distribution utilities to procure power supply for their captive market through a competitive selection process. It repeals DC2015-06-0008, DC2018-02-0003, DC2021-09-0030 and DC2022-06-0027 once the ERC's guidelines take effect. DC2025-10-0022 later amended it.
notes: Scouted from desk research (high confidence). Date from the NARO register and DC2025-10-0022; date in force not found. Repealing clause checked by OCR; the repeal is conditional on the ERC guidelines (Res. 16 s.2023), whose date and effectivity were not found. Repealed circulars other than DC2018-02-0003 are not rows. ERC companion rule Res. 16 s.2023 is not a row.

title_original: Prescribing Policies to Enhance the Procurement of Power Supply by Distribution Utilities for the Captive Market, Amending and Supplementing for this Purpose DC2023-06-0021
title_english: DOE Circular DC2025-10-0022 on enhanced power supply procurement by distribution utilities
summary_english: Sets further policies on how distribution utilities procure power supply for their captive market. It amends and supplements DC2023-06-0021 on mandatory competitive selection.
notes: Scouted from desk research (high confidence). Text read on the DOE page and PDF. Published 2025-10-26; the signing day was not read and the date in force was not derived.

title_original: Promulgating the Rules and Guidelines Governing the Establishment of the Renewable Portfolio Standards for On-Grid Areas
title_english: DOE Circular DC2017-12-0015 on Renewable Portfolio Standards for on-grid areas
summary_english: Requires distribution utilities and suppliers in on-grid areas to source a rising share of their energy from eligible renewables, at first by 1% a year. DC2022-09-0030 raised the annual increment to 2.52% from 2023, and DC2023-05-0015 amended the rules.
notes: Scouted from desk research (high confidence). Signing date as recited in DOE DC2020-10-0022 and DC2025-10-0020; date in force not found. DC2022-09-0030 (signed 2022-09-23 per news) is not a row yet.

title_original: Prescribing the Amendments to DC2017-12-0015 or the Renewable Portfolio Standards (RPS) Rules for On-Grid Areas

summary_english: Amends the Renewable Portfolio Standards rules for on-grid areas set by DC2017-12-0015. A separate circular of the same date, DC2023-05-0014, revised the off-grid RPS rules.
notes: Scouted from desk research (high confidence). Date issued as given in the UP Law Center NARO register (filed 2023-06-05); date in force not found. The content has not been read, so the summary says only what the title shows. DC2023-05-0014 (off-grid RPS) is not a row.

title_original: Promulgating the Guidelines Governing the Policy for the Conduct of Green Energy Auction in the Philippines
title_english: DOE Circular DC2020-07-0017 on the first Green Energy Auction guidelines
summary_english: Set the first guidelines for conducting Green Energy Auctions for renewable energy in the Philippines. DC2021-11-0036 repealed it (Sec. 22).

summary_english: Revises the guidelines for the Green Energy Auction Program and repeals the first guidelines of 2020 (DC2020-07-0017). The ERC sets the ceiling (GEAR) prices for each auction round by resolution. It was later amended by DC2023-09-0027 and DC2025-03-0004.
notes: Scouted from desk research (high confidence). Signing date from the PDF ('Issued on NOV 3 2021'); date in force not found. The amending circulars DC2023-09-0027 (2023-09-26) and DC2025-03-0004 (2025-03-07) are not rows.

title_original: Providing Specific Auction Policy and Guidelines for Non-FIT-Eligible Renewable Energy Technologies in the Green Energy Auction Program
title_english: DOE Circular DC2023-10-0029 on Green Energy Auctions for non-FIT-eligible technologies
summary_english: Sets specific auction policy and guidelines, within the Green Energy Auction Program, for renewable technologies that are not eligible for feed-in tariffs. It was later amended by DC2024-09-0028 and, according to NARO, DC2024-03-0010.
notes: Scouted from desk research (high confidence). Date issued as given in NARO, even though the number contains '-10-'; date in force not found. The amending circulars DC2024-09-0028 (2024-09-10) and DC2024-03-0010 (2024-03-25) are not rows. The DOE site lists a different title for DC2024-03-0010 (E20 gasoline), so check which circular amended this one.

title_original: Promulgating the Rules and Guidelines Governing the Establishment of the Green Energy Option Program Pursuant to the Renewable Energy Act of 2008
title_english: DOE Circular DC2018-07-0019, the Green Energy Option Program rules (2018)
summary_english: Set up the Green Energy Option Program under the Renewable Energy Act, letting end-users of 100 kW and above choose a renewable energy supplier. DC2026-01-0002 repealed it.
notes: Scouted from desk research (high confidence). Signing date as recited in DC2024-03-0009 and DC2026-01-0002; date in force not found. The official copy is on the old DOE site (not reachable); the source link is a secondary database. Repealed by DC2026-01-0002, Sec. 28, together with DC2020-04-0009 (RE supplier permits, 2020-04-22, not a row).

title_original: Promulgating the Revised Rules and Guidelines Governing the Implementation of the Green Energy Option Program
title_english: DOE Circular DC2026-01-0002, the revised Green Energy Option Program rules
summary_english: Rewrites the Green Energy Option Program rules and lowers the eligibility threshold for end-users from 100 kW to 50 kW, with an annual review toward lower levels. It repeals DC2018-07-0019 and DC2020-04-0009.
notes: Scouted from desk research (high confidence). Read by OCR of the PDF; check figures against the text. Published 2026-02-06; the signing day was not read and the date in force was not derived. DC2020-04-0009 is not a row.

title_original: A Resolution Adopting the Omnibus Rules for Customer Choice Programs in the Retail Market
title_english: ERC Resolution 13/2024, the Omnibus Rules for Customer Choice Programs in the Retail Market
summary_english: Adopts omnibus rules for customer choice programs in the retail electricity market. According to DOE DC2026-01-0002, it consolidates the ERC's issuances on retail competition and open access (RCOA) and the Green Energy Option Program.
notes: Scouted from desk research (high confidence). Date from NARO; date in force not found. It may supersede ERC Res. 08 s.2021 (GEOP rules, 2021-04-22, not a row); not yet checked. Which DOE circulars it implements was not checked, so 'implements' is empty.

title_original: Declaring the Commercial Operations Date of Retail Competition and Open Access (RCOA) and Green Energy Option Program (GEOP) in Mindanao
title_english: DOE Circular DC2024-03-0009 declaring commercial operations of RCOA and GEOP in Mindanao
summary_english: Sets 2024-03-26 as the start of commercial operations of retail competition and open access (RCOA) and the Green Energy Option Program in the Mindanao grid. This extends to Mindanao the retail choice that began elsewhere in 2012 under DC2012-05-0005.
notes: Scouted from desk research (high confidence). Read by OCR of the PDF. The DOE page heading shows a wrong title (petroleum allowances); the PDF and NARO are correct. Date in force of the circular itself not found. 'implements' points to EPIRA because RCOA rests on its Sec. 31.

title_original: Guidelines on Virtual Power Purchase Agreements
title_english: DOE Circular DC2025-10-0024, the Guidelines on Virtual Power Purchase Agreements
summary_english: Sets guidelines for virtual power purchase agreements (VPPAs), which are contracts to buy voluntary renewable energy certificates. Power still flows through the WESM or other regulated channels, and VPPAs are recognised as PPAs for financing.
notes: Scouted from desk research (high confidence). Date from the PDF (OCR) and Enviliance; date in force not found. Part of the description rests on draft-stage reporting; check it against the final text.

title_original: Adopting the Amendments to the Rules Enabling the Net-Metering Program for Renewable Energy
title_english: ERC Resolution 6/2019, the Amended Net-Metering Rules
summary_english: Amends the ERC's rules for net metering of renewable energy systems, first adopted by Res. 9 s.2013. Net metering covers systems of up to 100 kW. ERC Res. 15 s.2025 later amended these rules.
notes: Scouted from desk research (medium confidence). Date and title as recited in DOE DC2020-10-0022 and DC2024-08-0025. The ERC site is blocked (Cloudflare), so the ERC text was not seen and the source link is a DOE circular that cites it. ERC Res. 9 s.2013 (2013-05-27), the original rules, is not a row. Date in force not found.

title_original: A Resolution Amending ERC Resolution No. 6, Series of 2019 (Amended Net-Metering Rules)
title_english: ERC Resolution 15/2025 amending the Amended Net-Metering Rules
summary_english: Amends the ERC's Amended Net-Metering Rules of 2019 (Res. 6 s.2019). What it changes is not yet known, because the resolution is known only from a recital in DOE DC2025-10-0020.
notes: Scouted from desk research (medium confidence). Known only from the recital in DOE DC2025-10-0020; the ERC text, its exact title and its date in force were not seen. The source link is the DOE circular that cites it.

title_original: Prescribing the Policies to Enhance the Net-Metering Program for Renewable Energy Systems
title_english: DOE Circular DC2020-10-0022 enhancing the net-metering program
summary_english: Sets DOE policies to enhance the net-metering program for renewable energy systems. It was later amended by DC2024-08-0025 and supplemented by DC2025-10-0020.
notes: Scouted from desk research (high confidence). Date as recited in DC2024-08-0025 and DC2025-10-0020. Published 2021-02-24; the date in force was not derived.

title_original: Prescribing Further Policies to Enhance the Net-Metering Program for Renewable Energy Systems, Amending for This Purpose DC2020-10-0022
title_english: DOE Circular DC2024-08-0025 on further net-metering policies
summary_english: Sets further policies for the net-metering program, covering the banking of net-metering credits and the REC meter. It amends DC2020-10-0022.
notes: Scouted from desk research (high confidence). Date from the PDF ('AUG 19 2024') and NARO; date in force not found. Content as described in DC2025-10-0020; check the changes to credit banking and the REC meter against the text.

title_original: Supplemental Policy to the Net-Metering Program Integrating Renewable Energy Certificate Trading and Multi-Site and Aggregate Net-Metering to Enhance Participant Benefits and Market Access
title_english: DOE Circular DC2025-10-0020 on REC trading and multi-site net metering
summary_english: Adds renewable energy certificate (REC) trading and multi-site and aggregate net metering to the net-metering program. RECs from own use go to the end-user, RECs from exported power go to the distribution utility, and RECs can be traded on the Renewable Energy Market. Credits can be shared across one user's accounts in the same franchise area.
notes: Scouted from desk research (high confidence). Published 2025-10-19; the signing day was not read and the date in force was not derived. Linked as 'amends' DC2020-10-0022 following the scouting report's convention, but the text supplements that circular rather than amending its wording; reviewers should agree the convention and the link_basis.

title_original: Prescribing the Policy and General Framework on the Expanded Roof-Mounted Solar Program in the Philippines
title_english: DOE Circular DC2023-12-0035 on the Expanded Roof-Mounted Solar Program
summary_english: Sets the policy and general framework for the Expanded Roof-Mounted Solar Program, covering rooftop leasing and third-party business models. The program counts toward compliance with the Energy Efficiency Act.
notes: Scouted from desk research (high confidence). Read by OCR of the PDF. Takes effect on publication (2024-01-03); the signing day is blank in the copy. The DOE page shows a mismatched second title.

title_original: Policy Guidelines for Self-Generating Facility Zero-Export Solar Systems and Micro-Solar Systems for Own-Use
title_english: DOE Circular DC2026-08-0017 on zero-export and micro-solar systems for own use
summary_english: Sets simpler policy guidelines for self-generating solar systems for own use that do not export to the grid (zero-export) and for micro-solar systems. It asks the ERC to issue rules within 90 days.
notes: Scouted from desk research (high confidence). Takes effect on publication, but the publication date was not read; signing day not read. Check whether the ERC has issued its rules.

title_original: DOE Advisory on the moratorium on endorsements for greenfield coal-fired power projects
title_english: DOE advisory on the moratorium on greenfield coal power projects
summary_english: Stops DOE endorsements for new greenfield coal-fired power projects; expansions of existing plants and committed projects are excluded. A 2025 advisory widened the exemptions, and the DOE said in 2026-05 that the moratorium stays.
notes: Scouted from desk research (medium confidence). Announced 2020-10-27 and applied from then (date_in_force); the written advisory is dated 2020-12-22 and was released 2021-01-11 (news). The exact title and a DOE URL were not confirmed, so title_original is descriptive; old DOE node links now return a 'Page Not Found' page with HTTP 200. The legal force of an unnumbered advisory should be confirmed.

title_original: DOE Advisory clarifying the coverage of the coal moratorium policy
title_english: DOE advisory clarifying the coverage of the coal moratorium
summary_english: Clarifies which projects the 2020 coal moratorium covers and widens the exemptions. According to news reports, off-grid projects, own-use or self-generation, critical-mineral processing and on-grid projects needed to avoid supply shortfalls are exempt.
notes: Scouted from desk research (medium confidence). Advisory text not seen; content from news reports. Exact title and date in force not confirmed, so title_original is descriptive. 'amends' is our reading: it narrows the 2020 advisory without replacing it, so link_basis 'implied by successor' needs review. CEED and others criticised it; the DOE said in 2026-05 that the moratorium stays.

title_original: Philippine Energy Plan 2023-2050
title_english: Philippine Energy Plan 2023-2050
summary_english: The DOE's long-term energy plan, published in three volumes. Its clean energy scenario targets 35% renewables in power generation by 2030 and 50% by 2040, with nuclear and offshore wind as options.
notes: Scouted from desk research (medium confidence). Drafted and consulted on in 2023; a revised edition was reported in 2024-07. The adoption date is not confirmed, the PDF is on the old DOE site (not fetched) and the new DOE site's PEP link is broken. Marked non-binding as a plan that is not a signed instrument; check. The companion Power Development Plan 2023-2050 is not a row yet (date unknown). Climate Action Tracker notes the PEP has no coal phase-out.

title_original: Prescribing the Policy for Categorization of Energy Resources and Technologies in the Energy Mix to Enhance Sufficiency of Generation, Adequacy and Reliability of Supply for Electric Power
title_english: DOE Circular DC2026-02-0005 on categorising energy resources in the energy mix
summary_english: Sets a policy for categorising energy resources and technologies in the energy mix, aimed at sufficient generation and reliable supply. It covers how the Power Development Plan is prepared and updated (Sec. 5) and how distribution utilities' power supply procurement plans and distribution development plans must align with it (Secs. 4 and 6).
notes: Scouted from desk research (medium confidence). Read from the PDF text layer; there is no clear statement of what it amends. Published in the Official Gazette 2026-02-19; the signing day was not read and the date in force was not derived.

title_original: Directing the Establishment of the Policy and Administrative Framework for Offshore Wind Development
title_english: Executive Order 21, s. 2023 on the policy framework for offshore wind development
summary_english: Directs the establishment of a policy and administrative framework for offshore wind development. The DOE implemented it through DC2023-06-0020, and the first offshore wind auction (GEA-5) followed.
notes: Scouted from desk research (high confidence). Date in force not found. DOE DC2023-06-0020 (2023-06-16, NARO), which implements it, is not a row yet. The ERC GEAR price for GEA-5 was reported as PHP 11.00/kWh in 2026-02 (news; resolution not seen). The topics fit loosely.

title_original: Policy on Allowing Generation Companies to Finance and Construct Associated Transmission Projects for the Timely Integration of Power Projects Critical to the Country's Energy Transition and Supply Security
title_english: DOE Circular DC2026-01-0001 on generator-built transmission projects
summary_english: Allows generation companies to finance and build the transmission links their plants need, for power projects critical to the energy transition and supply security. A companion circular, DC2026-02-0007, allows TransCo to finance and build transmission.
notes: Scouted from desk research (high confidence). Date from the PDF ('Issued this 07 day of January 2026', OCR); date in force not found. DC2026-02-0007 is not a row.

title_original: Electricity Supply Act 1990
title_english: Electricity Supply Act 1990
summary_english: The framework law for electricity supply in Peninsular Malaysia and Labuan. It requires a licence for every installation, public or private, including own-use generation (s.9), and is the basis for tariffs (s.26), Energy Commission codes (s.50A) and guidelines (s.50C) and licence exemptions (s.54). It has not applied in Sarawak since 1 September 1990, and since 3 January 2024 Sabah regulates electricity under its own enactment.
notes: Scouted from desk research (high confidence). Royal Assent 22 Aug 1990; Gazette 30 Aug 1990 (ST reprint as at 1 Jul 2016, read); commencement date not recorded. Suspended in Sarawak by P.U.(A) 272/1990. The federal instrument under which ST stopped applying the Act in Sabah was not located. Also amended by Act A1116 (2001; not a row). The Malay text is authoritative.

title_original: Electricity Supply (Amendment) Act 2015
title_english: Electricity Supply (Amendment) Act 2015
summary_english: Amends the Electricity Supply Act 1990 to give the Single Buyer (s.22B) and the System Operator (s.22A) a legal basis, with ring-fencing. It adds codes (s.50A) and binding guidelines and directions (s.50C), makes non-compliance an offence (s.50E) and sets up the Electricity Industry Fund.
notes: Scouted from desk research (high confidence). Royal Assent 30 Oct 2015; Gazette 5 Nov 2015; in force 1 Jan 2016 per the list of amendments in the ST reprint. The official LOM PDF path returned HTTP 500, so the source is the ESCAP Asia Pacific Energy Portal summary; replace it with the official text.

title_original: Electricity Supply (Amendment) Act 2024
title_english: Electricity Supply (Amendment) Act 2024
summary_english: Amends the Electricity Supply Act 1990 to remove the provisions on efficient use of electricity (Part VA). Those provisions move to the Energy Efficiency and Conservation Act 2024 (Act 861).
notes: Scouted from desk research (high confidence). Royal Assent 2 Jul 2024; Gazette 26 Nov 2024. In force 1 Jan 2025 by P.U.(B) 520/2024, seen in a search snippet only (the e-aset host was unreachable); check the commencement notice. Act 861 is not a row. Peripheral to power-sector rules.

title_original: Electricity Supply (Amendment) Act 2025
title_english: Electricity Supply (Amendment) Act 2025
summary_english: Amends the Electricity Supply Act 1990 to license the import and export of electricity (new s.22D), define "green attributes" and create a Market Operator (s.22C). It received Royal Assent on 31 October 2025 and was gazetted on 18 November 2025, but no commencement notice has been found.
notes: Scouted from desk research (high confidence). High confidence for the text, low for commencement. Passed by the Dewan Rakyat 30 Jul 2025 and the Dewan Negara 9 Sep 2025 (press). Commencement is by ministerial notification, possibly in stages; no P.U.(B) notice was found and the Federal Gazette portal was unreachable, so the status is pending. Check for a commencement notice. Applies to the Peninsula and Labuan only.

title_original: Energy Commission (Amendment) Act 2025
title_english: Energy Commission (Amendment) Act 2025
summary_english: Amends the Energy Commission Act 2001 (Act 610) to give the Energy Commission regulatory functions over electricity imports and exports. It was gazetted on 18 November 2025 together with Act A1775, and no commencement notice has been found.
notes: Scouted from desk research (medium confidence). date_signed is the Gazette date, taken from the ST performance booklet (seen in search results, not opened); the Royal Assent date is not confirmed. Act 610 is not a row, so there is no amends link. No commencement notice found; check alongside Act A1775. Replace the source with the official LOM text.

title_original: Renewable Energy Act 2011
title_english: Renewable Energy Act 2011
summary_english: Sets up the feed-in tariff system for renewable electricity in Peninsular Malaysia and Labuan: SEDA grants feed-in approvals, distribution licensees must buy the power, and tariffs are paid from a renewable energy fund financed by a levy. Sabah moved to its own Renewable Energy Enactment in 2024.
notes: Scouted from desk research (medium confidence). Exact Royal Assent, Gazette and commencement dates not checked (the FiT began in 2011). Source is the SEDA page for the Act; the Act text itself was not opened. Companion: SEDA Act 2011 (Act 726). Key subsidiary rules (not rows): RE (Feed-in Approval and FiT Rate) Rules 2011, P.U.(A) 385/2011, amended e.g. by P.U.(A) 366/2020.

title_original: Renewable Energy (Amendment) Act 2023
title_english: Renewable Energy (Amendment) Act 2023
summary_english: Amends the Renewable Energy Act 2011. Among other changes, it adds s.1(3), which allows the Minister to suspend the Act in parts of Malaysia.
notes: Scouted from desk research (high confidence). High confidence for the text; commencement not confirmed. Royal Assent 22 Jul 2023; Gazette 28 Jul 2023 (text read). No commencement notice was found, so the status is pending; check whether it has commenced. The new s.1(3) appears to prepare for Sabah's Renewable Energy Enactment 2024 (our inference). Other amendments not reviewed.

issuing_body: Minister of Energy Transition and Water Transformation (PETRA)
title_original: Renewable Energy (Amendment of Schedule) Order 2025
title_english: Renewable Energy (Amendment of Schedule) Order 2025
summary_english: A ministerial order under s.63 of the Renewable Energy Act 2011 that amends the Act's schedule. It extends the feed-in tariff period for biogas from 16 to 21 years, with effect from 28 January 2019.
notes: Scouted from desk research (high confidence). Made 1 Aug 2025 and deemed in operation from 28 Jan 2019, so date_in_force is earlier than date_signed. Covers biogas items (b)(i)-(iii). Earlier schedule orders (not rows): P.U.(A) 131/2022 (biogas cap from 5 MW to 30 MW), P.U.(A) 347/2020, P.U.(A) 222/2017.

title_original: Guidelines for New Enhanced Dispatch Arrangement
title_english: Guidelines for New Enhanced Dispatch Arrangement (NEDA)
summary_english: Sets up the New Enhanced Dispatch Arrangement in Peninsular Malaysia, under which generators without power purchase agreements bid into the Single Buyer's dispatch and are paid the system marginal price. It is also the settlement layer for the CGPP, CRESS and CREAM programmes.
notes: Scouted from desk research (high confidence). Registered guideline under s.50C of Act 447. v2.0 dated 17 Apr 2017 per the registration record; effective date not recorded. Revised four times (rows -REV1 to -REV4). The PDF at the URL is the current consolidated text (Pindaan 2025).

title_original: Guidelines for New Enhanced Dispatch Arrangement (Pin.2019)
title_english: Guidelines for New Enhanced Dispatch Arrangement (NEDA), 2019 revision
summary_english: Revision of the NEDA guidelines that allows solar power producers to participate in the arrangement.
notes: Scouted from desk research (high confidence). Version date 28 May 2019 from the registration record; effective date not confirmed. The URL holds the current consolidated text, which ST overwrites on each revision; this version's own text is not archived.

title_original: Guidelines for New Enhanced Dispatch Arrangement (Pin. No.2/2019)

title_original: Guidelines for Single Buyer Market (Peninsular Malaysia) 2018
title_english: Guidelines for Single Buyer Market (Peninsular Malaysia) 2018
summary_english: Sets the rules for how the Single Buyer in Peninsular Malaysia plans, schedules, procures and settles electricity. It also sets ring-fencing practices for the Single Buyer (Annex 2).
notes: Scouted from desk research (high confidence). Registered guideline under s.50C of Act 447; registered 18 Apr 2018; effective date not recorded. Revised once (row -REV1). The PDF is 32 MB and the first download was truncated.

Revision dated 1 Nov 2024 and signed 18 Nov 2024 (ST listing 22 Nov 2024); date_in_force uses the 1 Nov 2024 revision date, which precedes signing, so check it. Content of the revision not reviewed. The URL holds the current consolidated text, which ST overwrites on each revision; this version's own text is not archived.

issuing_body: Energy Commission (Suruhanjaya Tenaga), approved by the Minister of Energy Transition and Water Transformation
title_original: Grid Code for Peninsular Malaysia - Main Code
title_english: Grid Code for Peninsular Malaysia - Main Code
summary_english: The grid code for Peninsular Malaysia, made by the Energy Commission under s.50A of the Electricity Supply Act 1990 and approved by the Minister. It comes as a Main Code and an Additional Code (glossary and sub-codes) and took effect on 1 January 2026.
notes: Scouted from desk research (high confidence). Dated 28 Mar 2025; in force 1 Jan 2026. Appears to replace the Grid Code for Peninsular Malaysia KOD/ST/No.2/2010 (not a row), which the CRESS guidelines still cite, but no revocation clause was found in the first 30 pages.

title_original: Guidelines for Corporate Renewable Energy Supply Scheme (CRESS)
title_english: Guidelines for Corporate Renewable Energy Supply Scheme (CRESS)
summary_english: Sets up third-party access in Peninsular Malaysia: a renewable energy developer can supply a green consumer over TNB's network and pays the Single Buyer a system access charge. The charge was 25 sen/kWh for firm and 45 sen/kWh for non-firm supply at launch, and PETRA reduced it to 20 and 40 sen for RP4 on 29 August 2025. 51% local ownership is a licence condition.
notes: Scouted from desk research (high confidence). Registered guideline under s.50C of Act 447. First version effective 20 Sep 2024 (Skrine); no separate signing date recorded, so date_signed repeats it. Revised twice (rows -REV1, -REV2). The 29 Aug 2025 SAC cut was a PETRA press release (PETRA.100-9/1/4 JLD.1 (39); not a row); check whether a revision codified it. See also MY-DEC-2026-CAP.

title_english: Guidelines for Corporate Renewable Energy Supply Scheme (CRESS), second version (March 2025)
summary_english: Second version of the CRESS guidelines, dated 1 March 2025. The scouting did not record what it changed.

The URL holds the current consolidated text, which ST overwrites on each revision; this version's own text is not archived.

title_english: Guidelines for Corporate Renewable Energy Supply Scheme (CRESS), third version (December 2025)

The 'Pindaan 2025' label is on the current PDF; check that it belongs to this version and not to the March 2025 one. Content of the revision not reviewed. issuing_body: Ministry of Energy Transition and Water Transformation (PETRA)
title_original: CRESS Acceleration Package
title_english: CRESS Acceleration Package (fixed system access charge for early projects)
summary_english: Fixes the CRESS system access charge at 14 sen/kWh (firm supply) for developers and 4.02 sen/kWh for green consumers for 10 years from commercial operation, for projects that reach commercial operation by 31 December 2028 under contracts of at least 10 years. When it was announced, 11 developers and 8 green consumers (3,148 MW) were registered under CRESS. The method for setting the charge changes from RP5 (2028).
notes: Scouted from desk research (high confidence). PETRA press release of 18 Sep 2026 (Malay only) plus the ST system access charge and criteria sheets; the source URL is the ST charge sheet. Malay title of the release to be added. Effective date not stated. Projects that miss 31 Dec 2028 pay the prevailing charge, with no extensions. The ST page says the guideline text is 'to be updated': link the CRESS revision that codifies this decision when one appears.

title_original: Guidelines for Community Renewable Energy Aggregation Mechanism (CREAM)
title_english: Guidelines for Community Renewable Energy Aggregation Mechanism (CREAM)
summary_english: Allows a local energy generator and aggregator to supply nearby green consumers from community solar plants of 100 kWp to 2 MWp per 11 kV feeder over the distribution network in Peninsular Malaysia. The community access charge was set at 15 sen/kWh and reduced to 9 sen/kWh for RP4 on 29 August 2025.
notes: Scouted from desk research (high confidence). Registered guideline under s.50C of Act 447; first version, registration date not shown in the PDF, so only the year is given and date_in_force is empty. Applications opened 1 Jun 2025. The 29 Aug 2025 charge cut was announced by PETRA (not a row).

issuing_body: Energy Commission (Suruhanjaya Tenaga), for the Ministry of Natural Resources, Environment and Climate Change (NRECC)
title_original: Corporate Green Power Programme
title_english: Corporate Green Power Programme (virtual PPA for solar)
summary_english: A virtual power purchase agreement scheme: corporate consumers contract with new solar producers, settled through NEDA, while staying ordinary TNB customers. Applications ran from 9 May to 31 December 2023 for an 800 MW quota, with commercial operation targeted for 2025, and 22 solar producers (563.42 MW) were announced in August 2023.
grandfathered: Application window closed; signed Corporate Green Power Agreements continue.
notes: Scouted from desk research (medium confidence). Medium confidence for the launch date, high for the 2023 round. Launch on 7 Nov 2022 with 600 MW per law firms (Rahmat Lim). Award notice of 7 Aug 2023: https://www.st.gov.my/sites/default/files/2026-03/070823--Announcement-of-Successful-SPP-For-CGPP.pdf. No document number; the April 2023 information guide is not a registered GP/ST guideline. 'expired' means the application window has closed.

title_original: Guidelines for Solar Accelerated Transition Action Programme in Peninsular Malaysia
title_english: Guidelines for Solar Accelerated Transition Action Programme (Solar ATAP) in Peninsular Malaysia
summary_english: Replaces net energy metering for new rooftop solar applicants in Peninsular Malaysia from 1 January 2026. Exports are credited on energy only, at the energy charge for homes and at the average system marginal price for businesses, with caps of 5 kW (single phase) and 15 kW (three phase) for homes and 1,000 kW otherwise. NEM participants can join only by ending their NEM contract.
notes: Scouted from desk research (high confidence). Registered guideline under s.50C of Act 447; registered 30 Dec 2025. PETRA sets the policy and SEDA is the implementing agency (eATAP system; https://www.seda.gov.my/reportal/atap/). Successor to NEM 3.0 but does not revoke the NEM guidelines, so there is no revokes link. ST lists two copies of the PDF (with and without _0).

title_original: Guidelines for Solar Photovoltaic Installation for Self-Consumption in Peninsular Malaysia
title_english: Guidelines for Solar Photovoltaic Installation for Self-Consumption (SELCO) in Peninsular Malaysia
summary_english: Sets the rules for solar installations for self-consumption in Peninsular Malaysia, without credit for exported power. It replaced the 2017 guidelines on connecting self-consumption solar (GP/ST/No.13/2017). Under an Energy Commission notice of 31 December 2025, the standby charge of RM12/kWp and the battery storage requirement apply only above 1 MWac; the battery rule used to apply above 72 kWp.
notes: Scouted from desk research (high confidence). Registered guideline under s.50C of Act 447; in operation 1 Jan 2025; registration date known only to the year. Revised twice (rows -REV1, -REV2). GP/ST/No.13/2017 (Pin.2023), which it revokes, is not a row. The 31 Dec 2025 ST notice (Notis Makluman, https://www.st.gov.my/sites/default/files/2026-03/Notis-Makluman-31.12.2025.pdf) is not a row; the standby charge threshold was previously 1 MWp. A separate SELCO guideline covers Kulim Hi-Tech Park (2025).

title_original: Kenyataan Media - Jadual Tarif RP4

summary_english: Sets an average base tariff of 45.40 sen/kWh for Peninsular Malaysia from 1 July 2025 to 31 December 2027, against 45.62 sen approved in December 2024. It introduces customer categories by voltage, separate energy, capacity, network and retail charges, an energy-efficiency incentive for homes using 1,000 kWh a month or less and a wider time-of-use off-peak period. A monthly Automatic Fuel Adjustment (AFA) replaces the ICPT surcharge mechanism.
notes: Scouted from desk research (high confidence). ST media statement of 20 Jun 2025 (Malay). No gazetted instrument or document number found; the title is taken from the file name, so check it against the document. RP3 was 39.95 sen/kWh (press). The 3 sen/kWh monthly AFA cap without government approval is reported by the press only.

issuing_body: Economic Planning Unit (EPU), Prime Minister's Department
title_original: National Energy Policy 2022-2040
title_english: National Energy Policy 2022-2040 (Dasar Tenaga Negara)
summary_english: Malaysia's economy-wide energy policy to 2040, built around a Low Carbon Nation Aspiration 2040. It is a living document, to be reviewed every three years by a National Energy Council.
notes: Scouted from desk research (high confidence). Launched 19 Sep 2022 by PM Ismail Sabri (press). No legal force and no document number. The NETR builds on it.

title_original: National Energy Transition Roadmap
title_english: National Energy Transition Roadmap (NETR)
summary_english: Sets the path for Malaysia's energy transition, with a target of 70% renewable installed capacity by 2050 (up from 40% by 2040), no new coal power plants, and coal close to fully phased out of power generation by 2050. Phase 1 (27 July 2023) named 10 flagship catalyst projects and Phase 2 (29 August 2023) set the targets and pathway; it also signals a third-party access framework for the power sector.
notes: Scouted from desk research (high confidence). No legal force and no document number. Launch dates are from the press; check them. Deputy Prime Minister Fadillah Yusof said in June 2024 that coal would be halved by 2035 and fully retired by 2044, and reaffirmed this in July 2026; neither statement is a legal instrument. No separate public power development plan exists; the JPPPET 2024-2050 generation plan is unpublished, so this row is tagged power-plans in the meantime.

title_original: Electricity Supply Enactment 2024
title_english: Electricity Supply Enactment 2024 (Sabah)

It gives the Energy Commission of Sabah (ECoS) powers over licensing (s.8), tariffs, an electricity fund and safety, taking over from the federal Energy Commission in Sabah. Existing Energy Commission licences stay valid until amended or revoked (s.111).
notes: Scouted from desk research (high confidence). Assented to and in operation 3 Jan 2024 (text read). The title year (2024) differs from the enactment number year (2023). Paired with the Energy Commission of Sabah (Amendment) Enactment 2024 and a set of 2024 regulations (not rows). The overrides link records that Act 447 is no longer applied in Sabah; the federal instrument for that was not located.

title_original: Electricity (Amendment) Ordinance 2023
title_english: Electricity (Amendment) Ordinance 2023 (Sarawak)
summary_english: Amends Sarawak's Electricity Ordinance (Cap. 50) to make Sarawak Energy the statutory Single Buyer. It allows solar installations of up to 50 kW (previously 5 kW) to operate without a licence and sell surplus power, and allows special agreements above 5 MW.
notes: Scouted from desk research (low confidence). The date is when the Sarawak Legislative Assembly passed the Bill; assent, gazette and commencement dates are unknown and 'in force' is assumed. The Cap. A210/2023 number comes from a LawNet reprint listing seen only in search results; confirm it. Sources are press and Sarawak Energy releases; LawNet and Sarawak Energy were unreachable (000 and 403). Reportedly also lets solar producers sell to other consumers when the Single Buyer does not need the power. Cap. 50 is not a row.
